package_info.why_malicious: This report is a historical and conceptual overview of software supply chain attacks, referencing notable incidents (e.g., SolarWinds, Octopus Scanner) and attack vectors (e.g., malicious open source packages, backdoored tools, dependency confusion). However, it does not provide specific details or code snippets for any particular malicious package.

behavioral_signatures: Malicious logic injected into build systems or compilers
Malicious code present in third-party dependencies or open source packages
Backdoors added to widely used system administration tools
Malware that infects all software builds using specific development tools
file_indicators: Unexpected modifications to build scripts or compiler binaries
Presence of unauthorized or suspicious files in build environments
Unusual changes in third-party package files
network_indicators: Unexpected outbound connections from build systems or developer machines
Connections to attacker-controlled infrastructure during build or install processes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor build environments and package dependencies for unauthorized changes, unexpected network activity, and the presence of suspicious files or code. Employ behavioral analysis to detect anomalous actions during build, install, or runtime phases. Regularly audit third-party dependencies and use tools to verify the integrity of build artifacts and compiler binaries.
